changelog: New in v54: a system whose SD card was copied from a working system instead of being properly reset now repairs itself. Such a unit could look normal but never connect to the secure remote-access link, and until now no restart or update could fix it. Installing this update also performs the repair: the system gets its own new secure link and finishes the setup by itself. There is nothing to do beyond the normal update; your Comfort settings and alarm are not affected. New in v53: the Config Files page now includes a link to the Owner Support Guide -- it explains what each on-screen message means, what you can safely do yourself, and how to use AI (such as Claude, ChatGPT or DeepSeek) to do more with your system: set up your own automations, dashboards and phone notifications using the Comfort entities. Nothing about the alarm or your settings changes. This update also includes every change from v52, listed here in full: Storage-card health checks now run between restarts: the card is checked every hour and a small write test runs once a day, so a card that starts failing is noticed the same day instead of at the next restart. If Home Assistant offers a software update while the card is already reporting a problem, the system now warns you not to install it yet: you get an on-screen notice saying so, and Cytech is emailed automatically -- a Home Assistant update writes a large amount of data and could make a failing card worse. The warning is about the Home Assistant update offered under Settings > System > Updates only; your Comfort system and its Check for Update keep working normally. When the card is healthy, nothing changes and no warning appears. If a card problem is found, the warnings now also remind you to save a backup copy of your system to your PC or Google Drive while it is still working. Alert-email setup is now fully automatic: a new system installs its email account by itself, and if you press Register before that has finished, it simply tells you to try again in a few minutes -- no installer visit is ever needed.
details: v54 carries the complete v53 change set and, through it, every change from v52; both are restated in full below after this section, and nothing in either was reversed or superseded. v53 was withdrawn before any fleet release and ships inside v54 instead, so units that took the brief v53 preview and units still on v52 both receive this update. v54 is the fleet release of the bench revision 54a (the shipped payload bytes are the bench-verified ones; the only payload change from v53 is first_boot.sh). Fake-provisioned provisioning repair. first_boot.sh: two new helpers, tailscale_backend_state() and start_tailscale_addon(), query and start the Tailscale addon from inside the Advanced SSH addon -- the addon's own $SUPERVISOR_TOKEN, because Core-container Supervisor calls can return 401 on some units -- with ConnectTimeout=10; an unreachable addon reads as not Running. The maintenance branch, which an already-initialised unit takes on every boot, replaced its old NeedsLogin re-auth / Running / else chain: if the backend is not Running it starts the addon and re-probes up to 8 times at 15 s (about 2 minutes, enough to ride out an HA OS update recreating the addon container). If it reaches Running, the existing URL-vs-external_url check runs unchanged. If it never does, the completion flag is provably false: the pass removes .zero_touch_completed and .dev_reset_mode, the baked SSH key pair and QR, writes 'Initializing Secure Link...' to device_id.txt, and falls through into the fresh-provisioning path in the same pass. That path sees no Running identity, wipes tailscaled.state, registers a new node with a freshly minted auth key, and finish_firstboot rewrites device_id.txt, external_url and the QR. Zero owner steps beyond installing the update -- the update's own Core restart (first_boot.sh changed, FIRSTBOOT_CHANGED) is what re-runs the script. Offline verification: bash -n; decision-tree harness against the extracted script bytes, five cases -- healthy Running (no repair, flag kept, normal exit), persistent NeedsLogin (8 addon starts, full repair, fall-through), addon unreachable (full repair), transient Starting->Running on the third probe (2 starts, no repair, normal exit), and Running with a URL mismatch (existing maintenance_repair path). Bench verification: PENDING for the 54a round. v53 was withdrawn before any fleet release; its change ships here unchanged. It corresponded to the bench revision 53b, whose payload bytes are unchanged in v54. Owner Support Guide link on the Config Files page. (1) dashboards/system.yaml: the Remote Support Access card gains an 'Owner Support Guide' paragraph -- what each message means, what you can safely do yourself, and 'how to use AI to do more with your system' (automations, your own dashboards, Comfort entities), the AI phrase in bold -- linking to https://github.com/slychiu/ComfortHA-yaml/blob/main/SUPPORT.md. The guide is a public-repo document, not updater-deployed, so only the link ships in this release. The same main-line commit expanded the guide: section 9 'Doing more with your system' teaches the owner to ask an AI assistant (paste-able prompt carrying the alarm entity, arm scripts, zone binary sensors, bypass controls and battery sensors) to build automations and their own dashboards, and restates the safety rules (do not edit the Cytech pages, .storage or the shipped automations; never give an assistant the remote link, login or PIN). (2) packages/cytech.yaml: comment-only bump so cytech_update.sh's auto-restart trigger fires -- without it a dashboards/system.yaml-only payload would not restart Core, and the YAML-mode dashboard would keep rendering the old page. Offline verification: both YAML files parse (pyyaml, UTF-8); the link and the bolded AI wording are present in the card. Bench verification: PASSED on cytech.local 2026-10-17 via the real owner flow -- Check -> Update Now through the Supervisor core-proxy service, from a local mirror built from the tag's blobs: v52 -> 53b, 27/27 files applied, Core auto-restarted each round, pending cleared. Deployed files byte-identical to the committed blobs (dashboards/system.yaml 7ab856be05b2d36d21d9ac908deeb3a2, packages/cytech.yaml eb0ffda0ed017b0f37ceeefe20f6a809); the bolded AI wording is present on the device; the post-restart 4-hourly network check ran normally. The bare-53 payload bytes are identical to the tested bench payload. (v52 change set -- included in this release, unchanged.) v52 is the combined fleet release of the three bench revisions 52a (SD-card early warning + update gate), 52c (alert-email credential self-provision; the owner is never sent to an installer) and 52d (backup reminder in every card-trouble alert) -- all three were confirmed on the bench and are promoted together; nothing in any of them was reversed or superseded, so all three appear below in full. SD-card early warning + update gate. Four files changed. (1) packages/cytech.yaml. New template binary_sensor binary_sensor.cytech_sd_trouble (unique_id cytech_sd_trouble_sensor, device_class problem) ORs the four trouble signals: sensor.cytech_sd_card_status == FAIL, sensor.cytech_sd_canary == FAIL, sensor.cytech_warning == REPEATED_RESTARTS, sensor.cytech_integrity_alert not in ('', unknown, unavailable) -- the gate and its warning text can never disagree about what counts. The card checks no longer run only at HA start: new automation cytech_periodic_sd_check (time_pattern minutes '23' -- hourly kernel-log scan, deliberately off the hour so it never stacks with the on-the-hour 4-hourly eth/config checks) reruns cytech_check_sdcard, and new cytech_periodic_canary (daily 03:41) reruns the 8 MB write/readback test (extra wear stays at canary scale, ~8 MB/day). New automation cytech_update_hold_on_offer: a template trigger that fires only on its expression turning true (no from_state bookkeeping), testing is_state(... 'on') for both update-entity id vintages in the fleet (older registrations keep update.home_assistant_core, newer ones have ..._core_update; entity ids pin at first registration, the v42b lesson; ids that do not exist simply read false; no regex -- Jinja has no 'search' test, caught offline). On a fresh offer it first RERUNS both card checks and waits 2 minutes (scripts fork; covers SSH-retry slow paths plus the 60 s command_line re-scan), so the gate judges the CURRENT card, not a stale morning result; then acts only while binary_sensor.cytech_sd_trouble is on. New automation cytech_update_hold_on_trouble covers the mirror case (trouble appears while an offer is already sitting un-pressed) with the same is_state offer condition and no fresh-check preamble. Both end in new script script.cytech_update_hold_notify: creates the persistent notification (id cytech_update_hold, title 'Do not install the Home Assistant update yet -- storage card problem detected', message carries the failing check's own text in the same priority order as the mailer) and calls the new INLINE shell_command cytech_alert_mail_updatehold. The gate can only warn -- HA offers no way to block Supervisor installing its own update -- and deliberately sends nothing when trouble appears with NO update offered: the v35/v42 alerts already mailed. (2) cytech_alert_mail.py: new kind updatehold, no result file of its own -- gate_message() composes the body from the troubled card-check files in priority order (sdcard FAIL, canary FAIL, boot storm REPEATED_RESTARTS, integrity) and falls through to the generic advice on missing/garbled files; copies follow the v41 rule (support always, owner when registered); subject 'Cytech: do not install the pending Home Assistant update: <unit>'. (3) cytech_check_sdcard.sh and cytech_canary.sh: header comments only (schedule now includes the periodic automations). Offline verification: YAML parse + structure asserts; all four new templates parsed AND rendered against mocked state layers (offer-check 12 cases incl. both id vintages, off, unavailable, unrelated addon update, none; sd_trouble 8 cases incl. SKIP and integrity-ts); mailer fixture suite 17/17 (priority order, generic fallback, garbled files, support-only, rc=2 no creds, legacy sdcard regression); bash -n on both scripts. Bench verification: PASSED on ems.local 2026-10-15 via a real Check -> Update Now from a local mirror (27/27 deployed-file md5s = committed blobs, core auto-restarted, version 52a, pending cleared). T1: new entities/automations loaded; sd_trouble off on the healthy card; an already-true offer template at restart did NOT fire (transition-only, as designed). Healthy offer: on_offer fired 12:44:28Z, reran both card checks 12:44:30, silent -- no notification, no mail. Trouble with no offer: injected FAIL -> sd_trouble on 12:49:23, v35 sdcard alert mailed 20:49:30, gate silent (on_trouble condition-blocked; noted: blocked runs leave no logbook entry and no last_triggered update). Trouble appears while an offer is pending: on_trouble fired 12:56:23Z -> sdcard + updatehold mails 20:56:30. Stale injected FAIL + offer: the gate's own fresh checks overwrote the stale file and the gate stayed silent -- it judges the CURRENT card. Injected FAIL (stub script with the real runner shape) + offer transition: on_offer 13:01:52 + on_trouble 13:02:23, mails 21:02:31 (sdcard) + 21:02:33 (updatehold, immediate path) + 21:03:59 (updatehold, after the on_offer 2-min gate); alerts log 4 -> 7, every line rc=0 support=sent owner=sent. A natural coordinator refresh mid-round restored the real offer-entity states and on_offer ran silently on the healthy card (unplanned at-rest evidence). Periodic automations manually triggered: both fired, fresh sdcard + canary OK lines logged. Teardown: real check script restored (md5 d26e21d7fe22297a6b2813f7f14a8c90), .cytech_secrets back on the fleet GitHub URL, offer overrides refreshed, notifications dismissed, final snapshot version 52a / sd_trouble off / all sensors OK / no pending. (52c.) Alert-email credentials self-provision; the owner is never sent to an installer. (1) cytech_register_email.sh: a press on a unit whose SMTP creds are not there yet now returns 'Alert emails are still finishing setup on this system -- this finishes automatically. Please press Register again in a few minutes.' The previous 'ask your installer to finish the email setup' text was a dead end for a freshly re-imaged unit (customer report 2026-10-15: the image predates the private-repo token, so the credentials never arrive and the owner had no path forward). (2) reset.sh: capture-time guard -- a refuse-to-capture ERROR when /config/.cytech_secrets lacks CYTECH_SECRETS_TOKEN, because clones from such an image could never set up owner alert email and nothing on a clone can fetch the token afterwards. (3) packages/cytech.yaml and cytech_alert_mail.py: comments only, wording brought in step. No first_boot.sh change was needed: ensure_smtp_credential (44d) already fetches USER/PASS from the private repo at every maintenance pass, and provisioning ends with one, so any unit whose .cytech_secrets carries the token self-heals with zero owner or operator action. Offline verification: yaml parse (pyyaml 6.0.3) OK; bash -n OK on both scripts; python ast OK. Bench verification: prior-copy reproduction + new-copy live check on ems.local 2026-10-16 (lettered round -- the functional file was installed in its committed bytes; no mirror deploy needed). T-A: stripped the token + SMTP creds + recipient from .cytech_secrets (byte-identical backup first) and pressed Register with the deployed copy -- the exact prior refusal appeared in both the result and popup files, rc=2 (the customer's report reproduced verbatim). Re-seeded only the token line and invoked shell_command.init_first_boot (the same call the HA-start automation makes; http=200) -- 'SMTP credential updated from private repo' appeared in the fresh log within ~20 s (line 360) and the pass ended exit 0; Register dry-run then reported creds=OK. Zero owner/operator action beyond the token. T-B: installed the committed register script (md5 0e84adaef8aefc3a8a41e849a1277d69) live and pressed Register on the no-creds unit -- the new message verbatim in both files, rc=2; then a full byte-identical restore (secrets cmp-verified against the pre-round backup, script back to 12afc1670f29d6f058585867c36842bb), popup file removed, notification cytech_register_result dismissed (http=200), final dry-run creds=OK. Residual gap, deliberate: an already-running unit from a pre-token image (like the reporting customer's) cannot self-heal -- the token must be hand-seeded once during remote support, after which the same maintenance fetch finishes the job; every image captured from a fixed master self-heals automatically. (52d.) Card-trouble alerts now also tell the owner to make a backup while the card still works. packages/cytech.yaml: the three alert popups (cytech_sd_alert, cytech_canary_alert, cytech_boot_alert) and script.cytech_update_hold_notify append the sentence 'Please make a backup of your system to your PC or Google Drive while it is still working -- Settings > System > Backups.'; cytech_alert_mail.py adds the same sentence as BACKUP_ADVICE to the sdcard/canary/boot letter bodies and folds it into GATE_ADVICE (the update-hold letter), so popup and email always carry it -- a card that dies otherwise takes the only copy of the system with it (the 2026-10-15 customer's card failed with the config existing nowhere else). Offline verification: yaml parse + jinja parse/render of all four templates against mocked states; mailer dry-run shows the advice on the sdcard/canary/boot bodies and inside the gate body. Bench verification (cytech.local, 2026-10-16): PASSED via the real owner flow -- Check -> Update Now from a local mirror; v52c -> v52d, 27/27 files, the two changed files byte-identical to the committed blobs (alert_mail 23f56efc2f2dc47d7d018c0cc6a1d7ca, cytech.yaml 7b295c387afd1c70f254c405a73d8ccc), core restarted, version 52d, pending cleared; all 17 cytech automations loaded. Live end-to-end on the deployed files: injected a labelled FAIL (stub check script, exact real result shape) -- sensor flipped OK->FAIL in ~50 s, binary_sensor.cytech_sd_trouble on, and two automations fired at 02:16:00Z: automation.cytech_sd_card_alert and automation.cytech_warn_about_offered_updates_when_sd_trouble_appears (HA OS + core offers were pending, so this was the real trouble-appears-while-offer-pending path). Alert log: 10:16:06 updatehold rc=0 support=sent owner=sent; 10:16:07 sdcard rc=0 support=sent owner=sent (bodies labelled TEST v52d round for the bench). Notification step: HA 2026.6.4 creates no states entity for persistent notifications (known quirk) -- the inline mail that follows the create step in both action lists ran, and the popup CONTENT is proven by rendering all four message templates extracted from the DEPLOYED yaml through HA's own template API against the live sensor states: sdcard/canary/boot each render as <message> + the sentence, the gate renders detail + contact + the sentence in order. The deployed mailer dry-run on a staged copy of the injected FAIL printed the full sdcard letter (closing sentence) and the updatehold letter (GATE_ADVICE sentence + 'What the checks report' detail), support + owner copies. Teardown: real check script restored (md5 d26e21d7fe22297a6b2813f7f14a8c90) and a fresh OK result written, manifest URL back on the fleet value, .pre_52d removed, notifications dismissed, final state version 52d / sensor OK / sd_trouble off. (Within 52, before release.) The gate's owner-facing text now names the Home Assistant update explicitly everywhere -- popup title, popup message, and the letter's subject and advice line -- and says plainly that it is about the Home Assistant update offered under Settings > System > Updates, while the Comfort system and its Check for Update keep working normally. Reason: the wording said only 'the update', which an owner could read as the Comfort config-files update (owner report 2026-10-16). Offline verification: yaml parse; jinja parse/render of the popup message against mocked states; mailer dry-runs (new subject and advice line on the updatehold letter; backup sentence still byte-identical to the popups). Bench verification (cytech.local, 2026-10-16): PASSED via the real owner flow on the promoted bytes -- Check -> Update Now from a local mirror built from this commit's blobs; 52d -> 52, 27/27 files applied, core restarted, pending cleared. The two changed files on the device are byte-identical to the committed blobs (cytech_alert_mail.py 8a5369e631232211d75b452884eb2351, packages/cytech.yaml 8799bf616154a6b3e5b2c44328b75c4a); all gate/alert entities loaded (both gate automations on, script.cytech_update_hold_notify, binary_sensor.cytech_sd_trouble off on the healthy card); with HA OS + core offers pending -- the gate's live condition -- the healthy card stayed silent, as designed. The reworded text on the DEPLOYED yaml: the popup title and all four popup messages rendered live through HA's own template API -- the title names the Home Assistant update, and the gate message renders the new lead ('Home Assistant is offering a software update'), the Settings > System > Updates disambiguation sentence and the backup sentence. On-device dry-runs of the deployed mailer (staged labelled FAIL, dummy creds, DRY -- nothing sent) print the new subject 'Cytech: do not install the pending Home Assistant update: <unit>' and the full reworded advice body with the 'What the checks report' detail on the updatehold letter, support + owner copies, and the unchanged sdcard letter. The email SEND path itself is untouched by this fold; live end-to-end sends on the same deployed code paths (4 labelled TEST mails, all rc=0) passed in the v52d round earlier the same day. Teardown: manifest URL back on the fleet value, .pre_52 removed, notifications dismissed, final state version 52 / sensor OK / sd_trouble off.
